teaching_note: Read these as dated doctrinal editions: record issuer, publication date, mission, intended audience and approval language separately. Doctrine states intended institutional practice, not observed success or present permission; compare the actual editions before claiming continuity or change [@ageint083; @ageint084].
title: Joint PSYOP Doctrine: JP 3-53 (1996 and 2003)

teaching_note: MISO is a doctrinal term, not a synonym for every covert message or for this course's prohibition on manipulation. Compare the dated document's mission and approval conditions with public-affairs responsibilities; an educator cannot infer authority from a public document or classify a notice as MISO merely because it is persuasive [@ageint085].
title: Military Information Support Operations (MISO): JP 3-13.2

teaching_note: A mirrored tactical manual is evidence of its text only after edition and provenance checks; hosting on Scribd does not establish authenticity, release authority or currency. Study historical institutional constraints and audience harms, not tactical procedures, audience exploitation or campaign construction.
title: Tactical PSYOP TTP: FM 3-05.302

teaching_note: A process diagram describes a proposed sequence, whereas an evaluation needs observations linking an intervention to outcomes and credible alternatives. Ask which approvals and assumptions the historical text specifies and which implementation facts remain absent; do not turn the sequence into a classroom influence plan [@ageint087].
title: FM 3-05.301: PSYOP Process Tactics and Techniques

raw: 18.5 Target Audience Analysis (TAA) and Susceptibility Mapping
teaching_note: The inherited heading names a historical practice; this lesson instead examines why language access, voluntary participation and independent judgment matter. Do not infer a person's vulnerability, motive or traits from group membership or build susceptibility segments. NGA's organizational page is not evidence for TAA; ICD 203 supports reasoning standards, not psychological validation [@ageint297].
title: Historical audience analysis: protection and evidentiary limits

raw: 18.6 PSYOP in Full-Spectrum Operations: Themes and Objectives[^86]
teaching_note: Separate a document's stated objective from the analyst's inference about a message and from measured audience effects. Similar themes may reflect shared facts, ordinary copying or public debate; neither resemblance nor disagreement establishes a coordinated influence operation. Historical mission language supplies no current authority to target learners.
title: PSYOP in Full-Spectrum Operations: Themes and Objectives

raw: 18.7 Leaflets, Loudspeakers, and Digital Media: Product Development and Dissemination
teaching_note: Completed offline case: synthetic record N1 says a museum opens at 09:00; N2 is an undated flyer saying 10:00; N3 is a dated authorized schedule confirming 09:00 but covering weekdays only. Applying [@sec:analytic-workflow], the filled result is weekday opening = 09:00 (N1/N3), weekend opening = unknown, and deliberate deception = unsupported; N2's missing date is the weakest link, with an old schedule a benign alternative. A withheld N4 identifies the flyer as last year's weekend notice, so revise from apparent conflict to different temporal scope; offer a dated, accessible correction and a choice to check the schedule, not an audience-targeting plan. CISA/NATO guidance provides defensive context, not evidence that any particular medium causes compliance.
title: Historical media products: accessibility and transparent correction
